customManagers.description: Track upstream Bun releases. This is the whole point of the repo: bun-nano exists to republish oven-sh/bun as a minimal image, so the pinned BUN_VERSION *is* the product. The pin lives in two files and both are matched here deliberately — one PR must move Dockerfile and docker-bake.hcl together, otherwise bake builds a different Bun than the Dockerfile claims and the published tags lie. scripts/bun-version.sh fails the build if they ever diverge. The built-in `dockerfile` manager is NOT enabled: it would open a second, competing PR for the `alpine:${ALPINE_VERSION}` FROM lines that the ALPINE_VERSION manager below already owns.
Keep the Alpine base moving too — it supplies libstdc++ and the CVE surface of every published variant. Same two-file pairing as BUN_VERSION, same reason.

packageRules.description: Auto-merge Bun minor/patch bumps. Safe to automate because ci.yml is a real gate, not a formality: it builds both published variants, asserts the running binary reports exactly the pinned version, and confirms upstream actually shipped musl assets for both architectures. A Bun release that would produce a broken image cannot reach main. Merging to main is what triggers release.yml.

A Bun major (2.x) gets human review. Note that Bun treats semver loosely — the Zig-to-Rust engine rewrite shipped as the 1.3-to-1.4 *minor*, so the automerge rule above is doing real work and the CI gate is what makes it safe.
